classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish four slope fields using gradients at a test point and along an axis.

content.prompt: Which slope field (A, B, C or D) corresponds to $y'=1-\dfrac{x}{y}$?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 12: four fields above the supplied blue answer
spec.description: Four labelled fields in a two-by-two comparison: A and B above C and D. Each field has integer-coordinate segments from −4 to 4, positive arrowed axes, ticks and numeric labels excluding zero. Source grey ordinary marks are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: A has direction 1+x/y; B has direction 1−x/y; C has direction 1+y/x; D has direction 1−y/x. At singular-axis sample positions, reproduce the source vertical direction marks without treating them as defined derivative values.
spec.answerVisibility: All four supplied option fields remain visible; no solution annotations appear.

answer.worked:
At $(1,1)$,
$$y'=1-\frac{1}{1}=0.$$
The segment must be horizontal, eliminating A and C.

On $x=0$, with $y\ne0$,
$$y'=1-\frac{0}{y}=1.$$
B has gradient $1$ along this axis, whereas D has vertical direction marks.

Correct answer: B.
